name: Woodcut
summary: A print from a block of wood with the white parts cut away; the result is flat colour, hard edges and visible grain.
how: Cut the block along the grain with a knife and a gouge; leave a line of 1mm to 3mm for the black.
Use one block for each colour and register them within 1 mm.
Print with a flat, opaque ink and leave the grain and the knife marks visible.
Keep the shapes flat, with no more than 3 to 6 tones in a print.

origin.note: The Diamond Sutra, printed in China in 868, is the oldest dated printed book made from woodblocks.

adoptions.via: Michael Wolgemut and Wilhelm Pleydenwurff design the 1,809 woodcuts of the Nuremberg Chronicle, which Anton Koberger prints with the text.
Suzuki Harunobu and his printers make the full-colour nishiki-e print on many blocks.
William Morris draws woodcut borders and initials for the Kelmscott Press, cut by William Harcourt Hooper and others.
Paul Gauguin cuts the woodcuts of the Noa Noa series with flat colour and rough cuts.
Ernst Ludwig Kirchner, Erich Heckel and Karl Schmidt-Rottluff of Die Brücke cut jagged woodcuts in Dresden.
André Derain and Maurice de Vlaminck cut woodcuts with flat colour and rough gouge marks.
